purpose: Option A (cheap, deterministic, no env/architecture change) to test the iter-7 reference-mismatch finding: add an analytic-reference jp_err metric to the eval harness and run it on the trained policy to see if the imitation-quality Gate-C item is satisfied when compared against the reference the policy was actually trained to track.

new_metrics: jp_err_analytic = mean(|dof_pos[0] - env.ref_dof_pos[0]|) per step — the policy vs the env's ANALYTIC gait-clock reference (what ref_joint_pos reward targets, updated every step by compute_ref_state). This is the reference the policy was TRAINED to track.
lateral_drift = mean|base Y - init Y| (frozen task_spec walking-task metric, previously unmeasured; threshold <=0.5 m)
yaw_drift = mean|yaw deg| (frozen task_spec walking-task metric, previously unmeasured; threshold <=15 deg/s)
harness_change.single_variable_change_vs_TASK_049: EVAL METRICS ONLY. Training config/algorithm/rewards/data identical to TASK_20260727_049 (commit d2cfd3f). The trained policy should be the same healthy walker; only the eval now reports the analytic-ref jp_err.
harness_change.py_compile: OK; all new metric names present; env.ref_dof_pos read guard added.

hypothesis_test.iter7_finding: jp_err(expert)=0.45 fails because the metric compares the policy against the retargeted expert clip, but the env rewards tracking an ANALYTIC gait-clock reference (ref_dof_pos). The two-reference-disagree floor was 0.422 rad (phase-naive), explaining the observed 0.450.
hypothesis_test.prediction: jp_err(analytic) should be MUCH lower than jp_err(expert)=0.45, and likely near or below the frozen 0.30 threshold — because the policy was actually trained (via the ref_joint_pos reward, scale 0.3) to track env.ref_dof_pos. If confirmed, the Gate-C imitation-quality item is satisfied when measured against the policy's TRUE target (Option A), without any retraining or threshold-lowering.

launch.note_on_retrain: This run re-trains (50min) + evals (~10min) because Gradmotion checkpoint-resume mount-path is still not integrated (the original eval blocker). The training itself is identical to prior runs; only the eval reports new metrics. A future optimization is an eval-only path, but that requires the checkpoint-resume integration.

next_iteration: Poll TASK_051 to completion (train ~50min + eval ~10min). Extract data/amp_eval/train_eval_report.json. KEY comparison: jp_err(analytic) vs jp_err(expert). Decision tree: (1) if jp_err(analytic) <= 0.30 AND stability/task metrics retained => the imitation-quality Gate-C item is satisfied against the policy's true target; document the reference-mismatch resolution and proceed to the remaining Gate-C items (dof_limit_viol safety, Sim2Sim). (2) If jp_err(analytic) is also high => the policy is not even tracking the analytic reference; pivot to Option B (real DeepMimic-style reference retargeting in the env reward). (3) Regardless, capture dof_viol and lateral/yaw drift (newly measured) for the safety + walking-task groups.
